nodes.title: the Clomorn signature
nodes.statement: The Clomorn system concerns objects called duthpons. There are exactly 6 of them: nakvint, rastrast, espanyr, yuksol, vorwren, vashtarn. One operation is written -. One relation is written >>, read as "yields to".

nodes.title: the Clomorn combination tables
nodes.statement: The value of x - y for every pair of duthpons is fixed by the table of the first operation. The pairs standing in the >> relation are listed in full.

nodes.title: closure under the first operation
nodes.statement: For all duthpons x and y, x - y is again a duthpon.

nodes.title: association of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all duthpons x, y, z: (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).

nodes.title: commutation of the first operation
nodes.statement: For all duthpons x and y: x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: a neutral object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a duthpon rastrast with rastrast - x = x - rastrast = x for every x.

nodes.title: an absorbing object for the first operation
nodes.statement: There is a duthpon nakvint with nakvint - x = x - nakvint = nakvint for every x.

nodes.title: reflexivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For every duthpon x: x >> x.

nodes.title: transitivity of the relation
nodes.statement: For all duthpons x, y, z: if x >> y and y >> z then x >> z.

nodes.title: agreement of the relation with the first operation
nodes.statement: For all duthpons x, y, z: if x >> y then (z - x) >> (z - y) and (x - z) >> (y - z).

nodes.title: the system does not have reversal under the first operation
nodes.statement: Some duthpon x admits no duthpon y for which x - y and y - x both land on a neutral object.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nakvint, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have self combination under the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For every duthpon x: x - x = x.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = espanyr, value = vorwren, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have cancellation in the first operation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all duthpons x, y, z: if x - y = x - z then y = z.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = nakvint, y = nakvint, z = rastrast, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have antisymmetry of the relation
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all duthpons x and y: if x >> y and y >> x then x = y.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = rastrast, y = vashtarn, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: the system does not have comparability of every pair
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: For all duthpons x and y, at least one of x >> y and y >> x holds.

verification.domain: every tuple of the carrier the axiom quantifies over
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = espanyr, y = yuksol, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: keldkeld duthpons
nodes.statement: A duthpon x is called keldkeld when x - x = x.

nodes.title: duthpons that shenshen
nodes.statement: Two duthpons x and y are said to shenshen when x - y = y - x.

nodes.title: tarnquil collections
nodes.statement: A collection S of duthpons is tarnquil when x - y belongs to S for every pair x, y drawn from S.

nodes.title: the wrensib of a duthpon
nodes.statement: The wrensib of a duthpon x is the collection of duthpons y for which x >> y holds.

nodes.title: the zelthra
nodes.statement: The duthpon rastrast is called the zelthra of the system. It is the unique duthpon that leaves every duthpon unchanged under -.

nodes.title: the iskvex
nodes.statement: The iskvex of the system is the collection of duthpons that shenshen with every duthpon.

nodes.title: the iskmux
nodes.statement: The iskmux is the collection of all keldkeld duthpons.

nodes.title: the wrenvash of a duthpon
nodes.statement: The wrenvash of a duthpon x, written [x], is the smallest tarnquil collection that contains x.

nodes.title: a pyrlorn
nodes.statement: A duthpon f is a pyrlorn when f >> y holds for every duthpon y, that is, when the wrensib of f is the whole system.

nodes.title: jentu duthpons
nodes.statement: A duthpon x is jentu when x - x equals the zelthra.

nodes.title: the geljen of a duthpon
nodes.statement: The geljen of a duthpon x is the number of duthpons in its wrenvash [x].

nodes.title: the ponazt
nodes.statement: The ponazt of the system is the collection of duthpons whose geljen is largest.

nodes.title: iskmorn pairs
nodes.statement: Two distinct duthpons x and y form a iskmorn pair when x >> y and y >> x both hold, that is, when each lies in the wrensib of the other.

nodes.title: the zelthra is the only one of its kind
nodes.statement: There is exactly one duthpon e with e - x = x - e = x for every duthpon x.

verification.domain: every object paired with every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Suppose e and f both leave every duthpon unchanged.
Then e - f = f, reading e as neutral on the left.
And e - f = e, reading f as neutral on the right.
So e = f, and the two suppositions describe the same object.

nodes.title: the zelthra lies in the iskvex
nodes.statement: The zelthra shenshens with every duthpon.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let e be the zelthra and x any duthpon.
Then e - x = x and x - e = x.
So e - x = x - e, which is what it means to shenshen.
Since x was arbitrary, e belongs to the iskvex.

nodes.title: the iskvex is tarnquil
nodes.statement: If x and y both shenshen with every duthpon, then so does x - y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the core
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y lie in the iskvex and let z be any duthpon.
Then (x - y) - z = x - (y - z).
Move z past y, then past x, using that each shenshens with everything.
So x - y shenshens with z, and the iskvex is tarnquil.

nodes.title: the wrenvash of a duthpon is tarnquil
nodes.statement: For every duthpon x, the collection [x] is tarnquil.

verification.domain: every object, then every pair inside its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is built by taking x and closing under -.
Closing under an operation is exactly the sealing condition.
The carrier is finite, so the closure stops after finitely many rounds.

nodes.title: the wrenvash is contained in every tarnquil collection
nodes.statement: If S is tarnquil and contains x, then S contains all of [x].

verification.domain: every sealed collection against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Every member of [x] is reached from x by finitely many applications of the operation.
A sealed S containing x is closed under each of those applications.
So each member of [x] is in S, by induction on the number of applications.

nodes.title: a duthpon is keldkeld exactly when its geljen is one
nodes.statement: x - x = x holds if and only if [x] contains x alone.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: If x - x = x then {x} is already closed under -.
So [x] = {x} and the geljen is one.
Conversely a span of one object must contain x - x, which is then x.

nodes.title: the geljen divides the number of duthpons
nodes.statement: For every duthpon x, the geljen of x divides 6.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: [x] is a tarnquil collection.
Its size is the geljen of x.
The claim is that this size always divides 6.

nodes.title: the wrenvash of a iskvex duthpon stays in the iskvex
nodes.statement: If x lies in the iskvex then every duthpon of [x] lies in the iskvex.

verification.domain: every object of the core, then its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The iskvex is tarnquil.
[x] is the smallest tarnquil collection containing x.
A smallest such collection sits inside any other, and the iskvex is one.

nodes.title: the iskmux is tarnquil
nodes.statement: If x and y are both keldkeld then so is x - y.

verification.domain: every ordered pair drawn from the ridge
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let x and y be keldkeld.
The claim asks whether (x - y) - (x - y) returns x - y.
Whether it does is settled by running the operation table on every such pair.

nodes.title: wrensibs are nested along the relation
nodes.statement: If y lies in the wrensib of x, then the wrensib of y is contained in the wrensib of x.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y satisfy x >> y and let z satisfy y >> z.
Transitivity gives x >> z.
So every member of the wrensib of y is a member of that of x.

nodes.title: the relation survives combination on the right
nodes.statement: If x >> y then (x - z) >> (y - z) for every duthpon z.

verification.domain: every ordered triple
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Let y lie in the wrensib of x.
Compatibility applies the operation to both sides at once.
Nothing else is needed, since z was arbitrary.

nodes.title: every duthpon lies in the iskvex
nodes.statement: Every pair of duthpons shenshens.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: The iskvex is defined by shenshening with everything.
The claim is that x - y = y - x for every pair.
That is settled by scanning the table for a pair that disagrees.

nodes.title: where every duthpon is keldkeld breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: x - x = x for every duthpon x.

verification.domain: every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = espanyr, value = vorwren, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where some duthpon reaches every other breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: There is a duthpon whose wrenvash is the whole system.

verification.domain: every object and its span
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case largest_span = 2, size = 6, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the relation reads the same in both directions breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: If x >> y then y >> x.

verification.domain: every ordered pair
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case x = rastrast, y = nakvint, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
One counterexample is enough. Note that the claim may still hold for many particular objects; what fails is the universal reading.

nodes.title: where the zelthra swallows everything breaks down
nodes.statement: It is not the case that: e - x equals the zelthra for every duthpon x.

verification.domain: the anchor against every object
verification.method: exhaustive enumeration by the reference implementation

proof.text: Take the case anchor = rastrast, x = nakvint, value = nakvint, read straight from the tables.
The two sides of the claim come apart on that case, so the claim cannot hold for every case.
